pieces.text: Lord, thank you for this meal and the people who cooked and served it. Bless them in their work today. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers Before Meals: Traditional Graces, Grace After Meals and Short Blessings

pieces.text: Bless us, O Lord, and these Thy gifts which we are about to receive from Thy bounty: through Christ our Lord. Amen.
pieces.source: F. X. Lasance, The Catholic Girl’s Guide (1906), “Short Form of Grace at Table,” p. 440

pieces.text: Bless, O Father, thy gifts to our use and us to thy service; for Christ’s sake. Amen.
pieces.source: The Book of Common Prayer (1928), Family Prayer, Grace before Meat, p. 600

pieces.text: Father, thank you for this food and for the people around this table. Bless the one who cooked it and the ones who will wash up. Help us listen to each other tonight. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers Before Meals: Traditional Graces, Grace After Meals and Short Blessings

pieces.text: Lord, many people will go hungry today. As we eat, show us what we can give. Jesus said, “I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat” (Matthew 25:35). Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers Before Meals: Traditional Graces, Grace After Meals and Short Blessings

pieces.text: Thank you, God, for our food, for our family and for today. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers Before Meals: Traditional Graces, Grace After Meals and Short Blessings

pieces.text: Give us grateful hearts, our Father, for all thy mercies, and make us mindful of the needs of others; through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.
pieces.source: The Book of Common Prayer (1928), Family Prayer, Grace before Meat, p. 600

pieces.text:
O God, from Whom all blessings flow,

These gifts Thou dost on us bestow;

We bless Thee for our daily bread,

Oh, may our souls by Thee be fed!
pieces.source: F. X. Lasance, The Catholic Girl’s Guide (1906), “Grace before Meals,” p. 439

pieces.text: Father, thank you for this food and for the people around this table. Bless the one who cooked it and the ones who will wash up. Help us listen to each other tonight. “Better is a dinner of herbs where love is, than a stalled ox and hatred therewith” (Proverbs 15:17). Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers Before Meals: Traditional Graces, Grace After Meals and Short Blessings

pieces.text: God of every good gift, thank you for this feast and for bringing us together. Thank you for the reason we are celebrating. Bless those who could not be here, and those who have no table today. “O give thanks unto the LORD; for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever” (Psalm 136:1). Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers Before Meals: Traditional Graces, Grace After Meals and Short Blessings

pieces.text: Father, thank you for each person you have put in this family, for the meals we share, the jokes only we understand and the ones who stayed with us through hard years. Keep us from taking one another for granted. “In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you” (1 Thessalonians 5:18). Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers for Family: Short Prayers for Meals, Bedtime, Peace and Hard Times

pieces.text: Lord, today two families sit at one table. Thank you for the parents who raised [bride] and [groom], for the friends who stood beside them, and for everyone who cooked and served this food. Bless what we eat and what we share, and let the friendship begun today last. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers for a Wedding Reception: Graces Before the Meal and Blessings for the Couple

pieces.text: Father, this is a small meal, and we are grateful for it. You taught us to pray, “Give us this day our daily bread” (Matthew 6:11). Give us enough for tomorrow too, and keep us generous with what we have. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers Before Meals: Traditional Graces, Grace After Meals and Short Blessings

pieces.text: God of all comfort, some people we love are not at these tables today. Hold them in your care, and let their love be part of this celebration. Bless this meal, bless [bride] and [groom], and keep us all in your peace. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers for a Wedding Reception: Graces Before the Meal and Blessings for the Couple

pieces.text:
Dear Heavenly Father,

With grateful hearts, we gather around this table, united in Your love. As this food nourishes our bodies, may our fellowship nourish our spirits.

Bless our conversation, kindle our laughter, deepen our understanding of each other, just as these meals continually remind us of Your endless love. Unite us in compassion and kindness, mirroring the unity found in You, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.

May our shared meal reflect the unity in the body of Christ, as grains of wheat are gathered to make bread, or grapes combined to produce wine. Bless this food and our fellowship, so that both might fortify us in Your service.

In Jesus' Name, we pray. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers Before Meals: Traditional Graces, Grace After Meals and Short Blessings

pieces.text:
Dear Heavenly Father,

We sit humbled before this meal, enjoying the blessings that you bestow upon us. We appreciate the earth’s bounty, your loving creativity demonstrated through the diversity of fruits, grains, and vegetables. We call to mind those less fortunate, and we ask you to provide for our brothers and sisters lacking. Let this food feed not only our bodies but also our souls, reminding us always of your nurturing care. With every morsel, let us taste your love, and with every sip, let us feel your abundance. May your divine providence never wane and may our gratitude for your providence ever swell. In Jesus' name, we pray. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers Before Meals: Traditional Graces, Grace After Meals and Short Blessings

pieces.text:
Gracious Father in heaven,

As we gather around this table, we pause to acknowledge your loving kindness. You've blessed our plates with bounty, nourishing our bodies, and connecting our hearts. Just like the sun nourishes the earth, your grace nourishes our souls. We thank you for the hands that prepared this meal and for the soil that bore these fruits. Lord, we ask for your blessing as we partake of this food, may it strengthen our bodies, fortify our minds, and uplift our spirits. As we taste the sweetness of fruit and the warmth of bread, remind us always of your unending love and generosity. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers Before Meals: Traditional Graces, Grace After Meals and Short Blessings

pieces.text: We give Thee thanks, O almighty God, for all Thy benefits. Who liveth and reigneth now and forever. Amen.
pieces.source: F. X. Lasance, The Catholic Girl’s Guide (1906), “Grace after Meals,” p. 440

pieces.text:
We thank Thee, Lord, Whose love doth give

The food whereby Thy creatures live.

Oh, grant us when this life is o’er

To dwell with Thee forevermore!
pieces.source: F. X. Lasance, The Catholic Girl’s Guide (1906), “Grace after Meals,” p. 439

pieces.text: We give Thee thanks, O Almighty God, for all Thy mercies. Who livest and reignest world without end. Amen.
pieces.source: A Manual of Prayers for the Use of the Catholic Laity (1888), Grace before and after Meals, p. 58

pieces.text: Almighty God, Father of mercies and giver of all comfort; Deal graciously, we pray thee, with all those who mourn, that, casting every care on thee, they may know the consolation of thy love; through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.
pieces.source: The Book of Common Prayer (1928), At the Burial of a Child

pieces.text: Eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord, and let perpetual light shine upon them. May they rest in peace. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers for a Funeral: Opening, Committal and Closing Prayers for the Service

pieces.text: Lord, we give [name] back to you. We lay [his or her] body in the ground in the hope of the resurrection, and we leave [him or her] in your keeping. Go home with this family tonight. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for a Funeral Service: Invocations to Read Aloud

pieces.text: Lord, you knew [name] better than any of us did, and you are just and merciful. We leave [him or her] in your hands. Comfort all who loved [him or her], and draw each of us closer to you. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers for a Funeral: Opening, Committal and Closing Prayers for the Service

pieces.text: Father, [name]’s illness was long, and the last months were hard for [him or her] and for everyone who cared for [him or her]. Thank you that the pain is over. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers for a Funeral: Final Prayers, Blessings and a Prayer at the Grave

pieces.text: Lord, [name]’s life was far too short, and everything in us says this is wrong. We do not pretend to understand. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers for a Funeral: Final Prayers, Blessings and a Prayer at the Grave

pieces.text: God of mercy, you knew [name] completely, better than any of us did. We entrust [him or her] to your mercy and your justice, and we thank you for every good thing [he or she] brought into our lives. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers for a Funeral: Final Prayers, Blessings and a Prayer at the Grave

pieces.text: O Lord Jesus Christ, who by thy death didst take away the sting of death; Grant unto us thy servants so to follow in faith where thou hast led the way, that we may at length fall asleep peacefully in thee, and awake up after thy likeness; through thy mercy, who livest with the Father and the Holy Ghost, one God, world without end. Amen.
pieces.source: The Book of Common Prayer (1928), The Order for the Burial of the Dead

pieces.text: Into thy hands, O merciful Saviour, we commend the soul of thy servant, now departed from the body. Acknowledge, we humbly beseech thee, a sheep of thine own fold, a lamb of thine own flock, a sinner of thine own redeeming. Receive him into the arms of thy mercy, into the blessed rest of everlasting peace, and into the glorious company of the saints in light. Amen.
pieces.source: The Book of Common Prayer (1928), A Commendatory Prayer when the Soul is Departed

pieces.text: Remember thy servant, O Lord, according to the favour which thou bearest unto thy people, and grant that, increasing in knowledge and love of thee, he may go from strength to strength, in the life of perfect service, in thy heavenly kingdom; through Jesus Christ our Lord, who liveth and reigneth with thee and the Holy Ghost ever, one God, world without end. Amen.
pieces.source: The Book of Common Prayer (1928), The Burial of the Dead, p. 332

pieces.text: Grant, O Lord, we beseech Thee, this mercy unto Thy servant deceased, that, having in desire kept Thy will, he may not suffer in requital of his deeds: and as a true Faith joined him unto the company of Thy faithful here below, so may Thy tender mercy give him place above, among the Angel choirs. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
pieces.source: A Manual of Prayers for the Use of the Catholic Laity (1888), The Burial of the Dead, p. 586

pieces.text: Lord, thank you for our mother, [name], who carried us, fed us and prayed for us long before we knew it. We give her back to you with thanks. Comfort her children and grandchildren, and let the love she taught us go on in our homes. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers for a Funeral: Opening, Committal and Closing Prayers for the Service

pieces.text: Lord Jesus, you said, “I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live” (John 11:25). [Name] trusted you in life, and we trust you with [him or her] now. We thank you for [his or her] faith, love and example. Send us home with the hope of seeing [him or her] again, and keep us faithful until that day. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers for a Funeral: Final Prayers, Blessings and a Prayer at the Grave

pieces.text:
We invite you to come and sit with us in our grief, to walk with us in our sorrow, and to be the unseen guest who comforts every heart. Let us feel your nearness in the kindness of a friend, in the beauty of a shared memory, and in the quiet stillness of this moment.

Open the eyes of our hearts to see you here. Let the warmth of your love be a tangible comfort that pushes back the chill of loneliness. Remind us that though we cannot see you, you are closer than our very breath. You are our constant companion, our ever-present help in times of trouble. Let the assurance of your presence be the foundation upon which we stand as we leave this place, in Jesus’ Name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers for a Funeral: Final Prayers, Blessings and a Prayer at the Grave

pieces.text:
Lord, you are the Light of the world. Today, we feel as though we are walking in a deep and disorienting darkness. The sadness is heavy, and the future looks dim. We ask you, a God who commanded light to shine out of darkness, to shine in our hearts now. Pierce through the fog of our grief with the radiant beams of your hope, your love, and your truth.

Be our lamp when the path ahead is unclear. Be our morning star, promising the dawn after this long night of sorrow. When our thoughts drift to despair, pull them back into your marvelous light. Help us to see not just the shadow of death, but the light of the eternal life our loved one now enjoys. Fill this room and fill our souls with a light that no darkness can ever extinguish, in Jesus' Name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers for a Funeral: Final Prayers, Blessings and a Prayer at the Grave

pieces.text:
God of eternal love, you are the source of all the love we have ever known. We thank you today for the incredible love we shared with our dear one. That love was a gift from you, a reflection of your own divine heart. Today, we declare that even in the face of death, this love does not end. It is a bond that death cannot break, a connection that time cannot erase. It lives on in our hearts, in our memories, and in the ways we were changed for the better.

Help us to feel that love surrounding us now, comforting us in our sadness and reminding us of the beautiful life that was lived. Thank you that nothing, not even death, can separate us from your love or the love we hold for one another, in Jesus’ Name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers for a Funeral: Final Prayers, Blessings and a Prayer at the Grave

pieces.text:
Almighty and loving God, we have come to the end of this sacred time. With reverence and deep love, we now commit the body of our beloved to its final resting place—earth to earth, ashes to ashes, dust to dust—in the sure and certain hope of the resurrection to eternal life through our Lord Jesus Christ. We also commit their spirit into your eternal keeping, where they will know perfect joy and peace.

But we also commit ourselves to you, Lord. We commit our grief, our confusion, our tears, and our tomorrows into your hands. We do not know what the future holds, but we know who holds the future. We lay all that we are and all that we feel at the foot of the cross, trusting completely in your plan for us, in Jesus’ Name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers for a Funeral: Final Prayers, Blessings and a Prayer at the Grave

pieces.text: Almighty God, we thank you for [name], who trusted in Jesus Christ and is now at rest. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for a Funeral Service: Invocations to Read Aloud

pieces.text: Lord, none of us expected to be here today. [Name] was taken from us suddenly, and we are shocked, confused and, some of us, angry. We do not understand, and we will not pretend to. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for a Funeral Service: Invocations to Read Aloud

pieces.text: Lord Jesus, you took children in your arms and blessed them. We have come to say goodbye to [name], whose life was far too short. We cannot make sense of this loss. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for a Funeral Service: Invocations to Read Aloud

pieces.text: God, we come from many places and many beliefs, but we are here for the same reason: we loved [name], and we miss [him or her]. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for a Funeral Service: Invocations to Read Aloud

pieces.text: O Eternal Lord God, who holdest all souls in life; Vouchsafe, we beseech thee, to thy whole Church in paradise and on earth, thy light and thy peace; and grant that we, following the good examples of those who have served thee here and are now at rest, may at the last enter with them into thine unending joy; through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.
pieces.source: The Book of Common Prayer (1928), The Collect “At the Burial of the Dead”

pieces.text: Almighty God, we thank you for [name], who trusted in Jesus Christ and is now at rest. We are sad, but we do not grieve “as others which have no hope” (1 Thessalonians 4:13), because your Son died and rose again. Comfort [his or her] family and friends. As we remember [name] today, strengthen our faith in the resurrection and our hope of seeing [him or her] again. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for a Funeral Service: Invocations to Read Aloud

pieces.text: Lord, none of us expected to be here today. [Name] was taken from us suddenly, and we are shocked, confused and, some of us, angry. We do not understand, and we will not pretend to. Jesus wept at the grave of his friend Lazarus (John 11:35); meet us in our tears. Give this family strength to get through today, and the days after, one hour at a time. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for a Funeral Service: Invocations to Read Aloud

pieces.text: Lord Jesus, you took children in your arms and blessed them. We have come to say goodbye to [name], whose life was far too short. We cannot make sense of this loss. Hold [his or her] parents, brothers, sisters and friends in your arms today. Give them the comfort no one here can give, and carry them when they cannot stand. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for a Funeral Service: Invocations to Read Aloud

pieces.text: God, we come from many places and many beliefs, but we are here for the same reason: we loved [name], and we miss [him or her]. Thank you for [his or her] life and for everything [he or she] gave us. Comfort everyone in this room, and help us to be kind to one another in our grief. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for a Funeral Service: Invocations to Read Aloud

pieces.text:
Eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord, and let perpetual light shine upon them.

O God, whose property is always to have mercy and to spare, we humbly beseech Thee for the soul of Thy servant N., which Thou hast this day commanded to depart out of this world: that Thou deliver it not into the hands of the enemy, nor forget it unto the end; but command it to be received by Thy holy Angels, and conducted into Paradise, its true country; that, as in Thee it hath hoped and believed, it may not suffer the pains of hell, but may take possession of eternal joys.
pieces.source: A Manual of Prayers for the Use of the Catholic Laity (1888), The Mass for the Dead, pp. 571–572

pieces.text: O God of spirits, and of all flesh, who hast trampled down Death, and overthrown the Devil, and given life unto thy world: Do thou, the same Lord, give rest to the soul of thy departed servant, N., in a place of brightness, a place of verdure, a place of repose, whence all sickness, sorrow and sighing have fled away. Pardon every transgression which he (she) hath committed, whether by word, or deed, or thought. For thou art a good God, and lovest mankind; because there is no man who liveth and sinneth not: for thou only art without sin, and thy righteousness is to all eternity, and thy word is true.
pieces.source: Hapgood, Service Book of the Holy Orthodox-Catholic Apostolic (Greco-Russian) Church (1906), The Order for the Burial of the Dead (Laymen), p. 370

pieces.text:
We need the peace that only You can give—a peace that the world cannot offer and our circumstances cannot take away.

We ask you to quiet the storm of grief within us. Silence the "what ifs" and the regrets, and help us to rest in the knowledge that our loved one is now fully at peace in Your arms. Let this heavenly peace guard our hearts and minds from being overwhelmed by anxiety and sorrow.

Pour out Your peace upon every person in this room. Let it flow like a gentle river, washing over our pain and refreshing our tired spirits. May this divine calm be a tangible sign of Your love for us and Your care for the one we have lost. Let Your peace rule in our hearts today, In Jesus' Name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: 12 Opening Prayers For Memorial Service: Simple & Powerful

pieces.text:
Lord Jesus, You prayed that Your followers would be one, and we ask for that unity today. We come from different places and have different memories, but we are all united in our love for the one who has passed and in the sorrow we feel. Please bind us together as a community of comfort.

Help us to set aside any differences and focus on supporting one another. Give us compassionate ears to listen, gentle words to speak, and open arms to embrace. Let our shared grief build bridges of understanding and empathy between us, rather than walls of isolation.

May the family feel the collective love of every person in this room, a powerful reminder that they are not walking this path alone. Let our unity be a beautiful tribute to the life of our loved one, who brought so many of us together, In Jesus' Name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: 12 Opening Prayers For Memorial Service: Simple & Powerful

pieces.text: Lord, help us remember what we agreed and do it. Give each person the time, energy and diligence for the tasks they have taken on, and let nothing we discussed today be wasted. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers for a Meeting: Short Prayers and Traditional Blessings to Read Aloud

pieces.text: Father, more decisions are waiting for us. Give us clear minds to weigh them, honesty with one another, and the humility to change course when we are wrong. Keep us from choosing out of fear or pride. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers for a Meeting: Short Prayers and Traditional Blessings to Read Aloud

pieces.text: Lord Jesus, you came “not to be ministered unto, but to minister” (Mark 10:45). Make us servants in this work, quick to help, slow to claim credit, and mindful of the people we serve. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers for a Meeting: Short Prayers and Traditional Blessings to Read Aloud

pieces.text: Lord, thank you for this time together and for what we decided. Help each of us do what we agreed to do, and bring us back together safely. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers Before a Meeting: Short Opening Prayers for Work, Boards and Teams

pieces.text: Father, we have talked, voted and made plans tonight. Where we decided well, give us the energy to carry it through. Where we decided badly, show us before it does harm. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers for a Church Meeting: Committees, Small Groups and the Grace

pieces.text: Lord Jesus, we did not all agree tonight, and some of us are leaving frustrated. Keep us from carrying this into the parking lot and the phone calls afterward. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers for a Church Meeting: Committees, Small Groups and the Grace

pieces.text: Lord, you have given us the care of this church and its people. Thank you for trusting us with it. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers for a Church Meeting: Committees, Small Groups and the Grace

pieces.text: Lord, thank you for the work in front of us and the people around this table. Keep us on the point, keep the meeting as short as it can be, and help us leave knowing who will do what. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers for Meetings: Opening and Closing Prayers for Work, Boards and Church

pieces.text: Father, we have talked, voted and made plans tonight. Where we decided well, give us the energy to carry it through. Where we decided badly, show us before it does harm. Help each person remember the task they took on, and let everything we do “be done decently and in order” (1 Corinthians 14:40). In Jesus’ name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers for a Church Meeting: Committees, Small Groups and the Grace

pieces.text: Lord Jesus, we did not all agree tonight, and some of us are leaving frustrated. Keep us from carrying this into the parking lot and the phone calls afterward. Where one of us spoke sharply, soften it; where someone felt unheard, let us listen better next time. Make us “likeminded one toward another,” so that “with one mind and one mouth” we may glorify God (Romans 15:5–6). Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers for a Church Meeting: Committees, Small Groups and the Grace

pieces.text: Lord, you have given us the care of this church and its people. Thank you for trusting us with it. Show us who is sick, who is struggling and who has drifted away, and send us to them this week. Keep us honest in the church’s money, humble in our authority and faithful in prayer for one another. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers for a Church Meeting: Committees, Small Groups and the Grace

pieces.text: Heavenly Father, thank you for bringing us together today, for every idea that was shared and for the patience we showed each other. Thank you for being with us, as you promised, where two or three are gathered in your name. Send us home grateful. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers for a Meeting: Short Prayers and Traditional Blessings to Read Aloud

pieces.text: Lord God, we have talked and planned, and now we need your direction. Show each of us the next step, and give us the courage to take it. “Commit thy works unto the LORD, and thy thoughts shall be established” (Proverbs 16:3). We commit this work to you. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers for a Meeting: Short Prayers and Traditional Blessings to Read Aloud

pieces.text: God of peace, some things said today were hard to hear, and not everyone got their way. Keep us united anyway, “endeavouring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace” (Ephesians 4:3). Guard us from gossip in the parking lot and bitterness at home. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers for a Meeting: Short Prayers and Traditional Blessings to Read Aloud

pieces.text: Lord, thank you for the work in front of us and the people around this table. Keep us on the point, keep the meeting as short as it can be, and help us leave knowing who will do what. Let each of us work “heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men” (Colossians 3:23). Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers for Meetings: Opening and Closing Prayers for Work, Boards and Church

pieces.text: God of wisdom, we have a decision to make, and none of the choices is easy. Give us the facts we need, the honesty to weigh them, and the courage to choose what is right rather than what is comfortable. “If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally” (James 1:5). We ask now. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers for Meetings: Opening and Closing Prayers for Work, Boards and Church

pieces.text:
Heavenly Father,

We come before You at the close of this meeting with hearts full of thankfulness. Thank You for bringing us together today, for the opportunity to discuss and share. We are grateful for the ideas that were exchanged and for the fellowship we experienced.

Thank You for Your guidance during our discussions and for any clarity that was achieved. We appreciate every contribution made and the willingness of each person to participate. We thank You for the technology that allowed us to connect and for the safety You provided for us during this time.

Lord, we are truly grateful for Your many blessings, seen and unseen. May we leave this meeting with a renewed sense of appreciation for Your work in our lives and in our endeavors.

In Jesus' Name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers for a Meeting: Short Prayers and Traditional Blessings to Read Aloud

pieces.text:
Lord God,

As we conclude this meeting, we ask for Your divine guidance in the days and weeks ahead. We have discussed many things, and now we seek Your wisdom to move forward in a way that honors You. Show us the next steps to take, both individually and as a group.

Illuminate our paths and make Your will clear to us. Help us to discern Your direction and give us the courage to follow where You lead, even if it requires stepping out in faith. May we not rely on our own understanding, but trust in Your unfailing guidance.

Give us clarity as we seek to apply what we have learned and decided here. May Your Spirit continue to work in us and through us, leading us in the way of productivity and purpose.

In Jesus' Name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers for a Meeting: Short Prayers and Traditional Blessings to Read Aloud

pieces.text:
Gracious Father,

As this meeting draws to a close, we pray for a continued spirit of unity and fellowship among us. Thank You for the opportunity to connect and collaborate. We ask that You would bind us together in love and mutual respect.

Help us to support and encourage one another in the tasks ahead. May the sense of teamwork and shared purpose we felt today continue to strengthen our relationships. Guard us from any division or misunderstanding, and help us to always seek harmony.

May we leave here not just as colleagues or group members, but as brothers and sisters in purpose, committed to lifting each other up. Let Your love be the foundation of all our interactions.

In Jesus' Name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers for a Meeting: Short Prayers and Traditional Blessings to Read Aloud

pieces.text:
Father of all comfort and God of all patience, we ask for a special measure of Your grace for this meeting. We know that discussions can be long and that perspectives can vary widely. We pray for the strength to remain patient with one another and with the process. When we feel our frustration rising or our attention wandering, please gently call us back to a state of calm focus and kindness.

Lord, give us hearts of understanding. Help us to truly listen to viewpoints that are different from our own, not just waiting for our turn to speak, but seeking to comprehend the reasoning and feelings behind the words. Clothe us with compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and especially, patience. Allow us to bear with each other in love, forgiving any offense quickly and completely. May our endurance honor You and strengthen our relationships. In Jesus' Name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers for Meetings: Opening and Closing Prayers for Work, Boards and Church

pieces.text:
We release our worries about the future and our striving to figure everything out on our own. We give it all to you. Help us to simply rest in Your presence and trust in Your goodness. Let our hearts beat in rhythm with Yours, filled not with stress or pressure, but with a holy and profound sense of calm.

May we carry this tranquility with us out of these doors and into our world. Let a quiet confidence in You be the foundation upon which we stand as we go from this place, secure in Your love for us, In Jesus' Name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: 12 Closing Prayers For Seminar: Simple & Powerful

pieces.text:
Father of unity, we thank you for the sweet spirit of fellowship we have enjoyed. You created us for community, and we have felt the beauty of that design here. We thank you for new friendships formed and for old ones deepened. As we depart, we pray that the unity we feel right now will not fade away.

Lord, help us to continue to encourage, support, and pray for one another. Remind us that we are all part of one body in Christ. Tear down any walls of division, misunderstanding, or comparison that may try to rise up. Knit our hearts together with cords of love that cannot be easily broken. May we be known by our love for one another, and may the community built here be a reflection of Your love for the world. In Jesus' Name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: 12 Closing Prayers For Successful Event: Simple & Powerful

pieces.text:
Gracious God, Sender of all blessings, we now lift up every person who is here. We ask you to look upon each individual with love and favor. As they leave this place, release a special blessing over their lives. Bless their families, their homes, and their work. Where there is a need, we ask you to provide. Where there is pain, we ask you to bring healing.

For those who feel discouraged, grant them a fresh sense of hope. For those who are weary, renew their strength. Pour out your wisdom upon them for the decisions they face this week. May they feel Your love in a personal and powerful way. Let them go forth knowing they are seen, valued, and deeply cherished by You. May Your face shine upon them and be gracious to them. In Jesus' Name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: 12 Closing Prayers For Successful Event: Simple & Powerful

pieces.text:
Faithful Father, Your presence has been so real to us in this place. We thank you for the moments of clarity, joy, and peace we have felt. Now, as we return to our normal routines, we ask for the gift of a strong memory. Help us to remember what You have done here. Help us to hold onto the feeling of Your closeness.

When our faith feels weak or when challenges arise this week, bring this event back to our minds as a powerful reminder of Your unchanging faithfulness. Let it be an anchor for our souls. We build a memorial in our hearts today, a stone of remembrance that declares, "God was with us here, and He is with us still." May we never forget Your goodness and the work you have started in us. In Jesus' Name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: 12 Closing Prayers For Successful Event: Simple & Powerful

pieces.text: Holy Spirit, be in this room before any of us speaks. Give us clear heads, honest words and patience with each other, and let what we do here be useful. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayer to the Holy Spirit: “Come, Holy Spirit,” the Veni Creator and Short Prayers

pieces.text: Lord, we are in different rooms and different towns, looking at each other through screens. Keep the connection working and our attention on each other rather than on our inboxes. Be with each of us where we sit. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers for Meetings: Opening and Closing Prayers for Work, Boards and Church

pieces.text: Thank you, Lord, for this work, for the people around this table and for what we have finished since we last met. Keep us grateful and humble as we plan what comes next. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers Before a Meeting: Short Opening Prayers for Work, Boards and Teams

pieces.text: Lord, we are tired, and this meeting comes at the end of a long day. Give us enough energy to think clearly for one more hour, and patience with each other when we are slow. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers Before a Meeting: Short Opening Prayers for Work, Boards and Teams

pieces.text: Father, thank you for everyone here who gives time to serve: in the nursery, the kitchen, the parking lot and the sound booth. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for a Church Meeting, Council or Prayer Meeting

pieces.text: Lord of the harvest, lift our eyes beyond this building to the neighbors who do not know you and the places where your church is small or suffering. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for a Church Meeting, Council or Prayer Meeting

pieces.text: God, before we turn to the agenda, we thank you: for this congregation, for prayers you have answered since we last met and for the people who have joined us. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for a Church Meeting, Council or Prayer Meeting

pieces.text: God, we are beginning something new, and we cannot see how it will end. Give us good ideas and the humility to hear better ones from each other. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers for Meetings: Opening and Closing Prayers for Work, Boards and Church

pieces.text: Lord Jesus, you said, “if two of you shall agree on earth as touching any thing that they shall ask, it shall be done for them of my Father which is in heaven. For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them” (Matthew 18:19–20). We are gathered in your name. Teach us to pray, give us faith to ask, and make us patient to wait for your answer. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for a Church Meeting, Council or Prayer Meeting

pieces.text: Father, thank you for everyone here who gives time to serve: in the nursery, the kitchen, the parking lot and the sound booth. “As every man hath received the gift, even so minister the same one to another” (1 Peter 4:10). Show each of us where we fit, and keep us from growing tired or resentful. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for a Church Meeting, Council or Prayer Meeting

pieces.text: Lord of the harvest, lift our eyes beyond this building to the neighbors who do not know you and the places where your church is small or suffering. Let our plans and our budget show that we care about them. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for a Church Meeting, Council or Prayer Meeting

pieces.text: God, we are beginning something new, and we cannot see how it will end. Give us good ideas and the humility to hear better ones from each other. “Commit thy works unto the LORD, and thy thoughts shall be established” (Proverbs 16:3). We commit this work to you. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers for Meetings: Opening and Closing Prayers for Work, Boards and Church

pieces.text: Lord Jesus, you promised to be among us when two or three gather in your name. Here we are. Teach us to pray, keep us from long speeches dressed up as prayers, and hear each request we bring for the sick, the grieving, our church and our town. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers for Meetings: Opening and Closing Prayers for Work, Boards and Church

pieces.text: Lord, we have a full agenda and limited time. Help us listen before we answer, say plainly what we mean, and keep to the point. Let the work we plan today be honest and useful, and “establish thou the work of our hands” (Psalm 90:17). Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers Before a Meeting: Short Opening Prayers for Work, Boards and Teams

pieces.text: Father, some of us come to this meeting worried or annoyed, and there are hard things to discuss. Keep our voices calm and our words fair. Help us disagree without contempt and leave as colleagues, as far as it lies in us to “live peaceably with all men” (Romans 12:18). Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers Before a Meeting: Short Opening Prayers for Work, Boards and Teams

pieces.text: God, this meeting brings difficult news: jobs, money or plans that will not work out. Give those who must speak the right words and those who must listen the strength to hear them. Show us how to look after one another in what comes next. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers Before a Meeting: Short Opening Prayers for Work, Boards and Teams

pieces.text:
We lay down the anxieties, worries, and distractions that weigh on our minds. Release us from the rush of our schedules and the stress of our circumstances. Replace our tension with your divine tranquility that goes beyond all human understanding.

We ask that your peace would guard our hearts and our minds. Let it be a shield against discord, frustration, and misunderstanding. May your gentle spirit settle over our conversations, allowing us to communicate with grace and kindness. Let this place be a sanctuary of calm in a chaotic world, a space where our souls can find rest in you. We breathe in your peace and breathe out our fears, trusting completely in your loving care over us and over this time together, in Jesus’ Name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for a Gathering: Meetings, Small Groups, Families and Events

pieces.text:
Almighty God, our protector and shield, we place this gathering under your divine care. We ask for your hand of protection to be over every person here. Guard our physical well-being and keep us safe from any harm or accident as we meet and as we travel home.

More than that, Lord, we ask for your spiritual protection. Shield our hearts and minds from the lies of the enemy. Protect us from discouragement, division, and doubt. Let no word of gossip or negativity take root here. We declare this to be holy ground, a space dedicated to you. Surround us with your presence, so that we may feel safe, seen, and secure, free to be open and honest with you and with each other. Be our mighty fortress, our safe place, in Jesus’ Name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for a Gathering: Meetings, Small Groups, Families and Events

pieces.text: We are here, O Lord Holy Spirit, we are here, held back by the weight of our sins, but gathered together in your name. Come to us, be with us, and enter our hearts. Teach us what we are to do, show us where we are to go, and work in us what we are to accomplish. Be alone the one who prompts our judgments and brings them about, you who alone, with God the Father and his Son, have a glorious name. Do not let us be disturbers of justice, you who love fairness above all. Let not ignorance lead us astray, nor favor sway us, nor any gift or partiality corrupt us. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers for Meetings: Opening and Closing Prayers for Work, Boards and Church

pieces.text:
Dear Lord,

As we gather here today, we humbly ask for Your divine presence to fill this space. Open our hearts and minds, Lord, that we may receive each word spoken with grace and understanding. Help us to lay down the barriers that divide us, the prejudices that blind us, and the fears that hinder us.

Just as rain opens the earth to receive the seed, open our hearts to receive Your wisdom and the insights shared by our peers. Let our discussions be fertile ground for growth, innovation, and the strengthening of our bonds. Teach us the art of listening—not just to respond, but to understand, not just to hear, but to truly comprehend.

Lord, in Your wisdom, guide us to be architects of bridges, not walls. May our meeting be a testament to the power of open hearts and minds working in harmony under Your guidance.

Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers Before a Meeting: Short Opening Prayers for Work, Boards and Teams

pieces.text:
Heavenly Father,

In this gathering, we humbly ask You to bestow upon us the gift of clarity and focus. Like the calm after a storm, quiet our minds from the whirlwind of daily concerns, allowing us to see Your path with unclouded vision.

Grant us the serenity to focus on our purpose here today. Like a lamp unto our feet, light our way through the complexities of our discussions. Let our thoughts flow freely and constructively, building bridges of understanding and cooperation.

May our hearts and minds be aligned with Your Divine wisdom, ensuring that every word spoken and decision made reflects Your love and grace. Guide us to be attentive to one another, fostering an environment of mutual respect and unity.

In Jesus' Name, we pray,

Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers Before a Meeting: Short Opening Prayers for Work, Boards and Teams

pieces.text:
Heavenly Father,

As we gather here today, we come before You seeking the blessings of mutual respect and understanding. In a world where every individual is a unique creation, help us to see the beauty in our differences and the strength in our unity.

Guide our hearts and minds to listen actively, speak kindly, and judge sparingly. Let Your wisdom be the beacon that lights our discussions, ensuring that they are fruitful and fulfilling. Grant us the patience to understand perspectives that differ from our own and the grace to respect each opinion as valuable.

May Your love be the foundation upon which our meeting stands, reminding us that in seeking understanding and respect, we echo Your greatest commandments. Help us to leave this meeting better than we came, united in purpose and enriched by our shared humanity.

In Jesus' Name we pray, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers Before a Meeting: Short Opening Prayers for Work, Boards and Teams

pieces.text:
Father of Light, we admit that we do not have all the answers. We come to you seeking your divine guidance for our time together. We ask that you would quiet our own frantic thoughts so that we can clearly hear your still, small voice. Grant us the wisdom to understand the topics before us and the discernment to make choices that honor you.

Please pour out your Holy Spirit upon us, illuminating our minds and guiding our tongues. Keep us from leaning on our own limited understanding. We pray for clarity in our discussions and unity in our decisions. May every conclusion we reach and every plan we make be inspired by you and for your glory. Cover this gathering with your presence and lead us forward into your perfect will, in Jesus’ Name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for a Gathering: Meetings, Small Groups, Families and Events

pieces.text:
God, our Rock and our Fortress,

We know that our journey as a team will not always be easy. We know that challenges, disagreements, and pressures will come. In those moments, we pray that you would be our unshakable source of strength and resilience. We ask not for the absence of problems, but for the courage and unity to face them together, hand in hand.

When we feel overwhelmed, remind us that we are not alone. Help us to lean on you and on one another for support. Turn our obstacles into opportunities to build trust, develop our character, and deepen our reliance on you. Let every difficulty we overcome make us a more bonded, more determined, and more faithful team. May the way we handle adversity be a powerful testimony to your faithfulness and strength working within us. In Jesus' Name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: 12 Opening Prayers For Team Building: Simple & Powerful

pieces.text: Lord, at the end of this school year, thank you for every lesson, every teacher and every friend. Keep what we learned, forgive what we wasted, and bring us back rested. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers for Students and Teachers: For Class, Study, Exams and Hard Days

pieces.text: Thank you, God, for today: for what we learned and for our friends. Forgive us where we were unkind, and keep us safe until tomorrow. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Back-to-School Prayers for Students, Parents and Teachers

pieces.text: We give Thee thanks, merciful God, for the instruction and direction which we have received. Grant us Thy grace that we may lay the lesson to heart and carry it into action, to Thy glory and our eternal welfare. Furthermore we pray Thee to pour forth Thy blessing upon our parents and superiors, our teachers and benefactors, and to recompense them abundantly for all the good which they have been the means of bringing to us. Through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.
pieces.source: Lasance, The Catholic Girl’s Guide (1906), “Prayer after Instruction,” pp. 438–439

pieces.text: Lord, bless our work today. Help us listen well, be kind to each other and learn something new. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Back-to-School Prayers for Students, Parents and Teachers

pieces.text:
Heavenly Father, You are the source of all knowledge and truth.

May our learning always bring glory and honor to You, the Giver of all good things, In Jesus' Name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers for Students and Teachers: For Class, Study, Exams and Hard Days

pieces.text:
Lord Jesus, You are our greatest example of love and compassion. You saw the person that everyone else overlooked.

Make our schools a safe haven of kindness for everyone, In Jesus' Name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers for Students and Teachers: For Class, Study, Exams and Hard Days

pieces.text: O Lord God and heavenly Father, bestow upon us the gift of Thy Holy Spirit, that enlightened by Him, we may understand aright and keep in mind all that we may learn that is profitable to us, and may both begin and end all things well to Thy glory, and in the name of Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.
pieces.source: Lasance, The Catholic Girl’s Guide (1906), “Prayer before Instruction,” p. 438

pieces.text: Almighty God, we beseech thee, with thy gracious favour to behold our universities, colleges, and schools, that knowledge may be increased among us, and all good learning flourish and abound. Bless all who teach and all who learn; and grant that in humility of heart they may ever look unto thee, who art the fountain of all wisdom; through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.
pieces.source: The Book of Common Prayer (1928), Prayers, “For Schools, Colleges, and Universities,” p. 42

pieces.text:
Heavenly Father, You are the source of all knowledge and truth. We come before You today asking for a special gift: the wisdom that comes only from You. For every student, please quiet the noise and distractions so their minds can be clear and ready to learn.

May our learning always bring glory and honor to You, the Giver of all good things, In Jesus' Name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers for Students and Teachers: For Class, Study, Exams and Hard Days

pieces.text:
We lift up every student and teacher who feels anxious or overwhelmed. Please calm their racing thoughts and soothe their worried spirits. Remind them to breathe and to cast all their anxieties on You, because You care for them. Guard their minds from the "what ifs" and help them to focus on this present moment, trusting that You hold their future.

When stress begins to rise, let it be a signal to turn to You. Help us to build quiet moments into our busy days to connect with Your peaceful presence. Let this peace guide our decisions, soften our words, and relax our bodies. May Your tranquility rule in our classrooms and in our homes, reminding us that we are safe and secure in Your loving hands, In Jesus' Name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers for Students and Teachers: For Class, Study, Exams and Hard Days

pieces.text:
Heavenly Father, You are the source of all knowledge and truth. We come before You today asking for a special gift: the wisdom that comes only from You. For every student, please quiet the noise and distractions so their minds can be clear and ready to learn. Help them to not just memorize facts, but to truly understand the lessons before them. Give them insight to connect what they learn in the classroom to the world You created.

For every teacher, we ask for Your guidance. Grant them the wisdom to explain difficult ideas in simple ways. Show them how to see the unique needs of each student and give them the right words to encourage and build up each one.

May our learning always bring glory and honor to You, the Giver of all good things, In Jesus' Name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers for Students and Teachers: For Class, Study, Exams and Hard Days

pieces.text:
Almighty God, You have not given us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and a sound mind. Yet, we confess that fear and doubt often creep into our hearts at school. The fear of failure, the fear of what others think, and the anxiety of standing in front of a class can feel overwhelming. Today, we ask You to replace that fear with Your perfect courage.

For every student facing a big test or a difficult assignment, build a holy confidence inside of them. Remind them that their worth is not measured by a grade, but by the fact that they are wonderfully made by You. Give them a calm heart and a clear mind to do their best work without being paralyzed by worry.

May our schools be places where everyone is empowered to be brave and to trust in Your strength, In Jesus' Name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers for Students and Teachers: For Class, Study, Exams and Hard Days

pieces.text: Heavenly Father, thank you for your word today. Do not let the worries of the week choke what was planted in us today. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers and Benedictions for a Church Service

pieces.text: Lord Jesus, you have fed us here, and now you send us out. Open our eyes to the needs of the people we will meet this week, and give us willing hands to meet them. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers and Benedictions for a Church Service

pieces.text: Almighty God, we do not know what this week holds, but you do. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers and Benedictions for a Church Service

pieces.text: Lord, we heard your word today. Go with us into our homes, our work and our schools this week. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers for a Church Meeting: Committees, Small Groups and the Grace

pieces.text: Gracious God, thank you for this hour: for the songs, the reading of your word, the prayers and the people beside us. We entered your gates “with thanksgiving” (Psalm 100:4), and we leave the same way. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers and Benedictions for a Church Service

pieces.text: Grant, we beseech thee, Almighty God, that the words which we have heard this day with our outward ears, may, through thy grace, be so grafted inwardly in our hearts, that they may bring forth in us the fruit of good living, to the honour and praise of thy Name; through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.
pieces.source: The Book of Common Prayer (1928), Prayers, Collects, p. 49

pieces.text: Direct us, O Lord, in all our doings, with thy most gracious favour, and further us with thy continual help; that in all our works begun, continued, and ended in thee, we may glorify thy holy Name, and finally, by thy mercy, obtain everlasting life; through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.
pieces.source: The Book of Common Prayer (1928), Prayers, Collects, p. 49

pieces.text: Almighty God, who hast given us grace at this time with one accord to make our common supplications unto thee; and dost promise that when two or three are gathered together in thy Name thou wilt grant their requests; Fulfil now, O Lord, the desires and petitions of thy servants, as may be most expedient for them; granting us in this world knowledge of thy truth, and in the world to come life everlasting. Amen.
pieces.source: The Book of Common Prayer (1928), Morning Prayer, “A Prayer of St. Chrysostom” and 2 Corinthians 13:14, p. 20

pieces.text: Lord, we heard your word today. Go with us into our homes, our work and our schools this week. Jesus told his disciples, “Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven” (Matthew 5:16). Help us do that where we live, and bring us back to worship you again next Sunday. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers for a Church Meeting: Committees, Small Groups and the Grace

pieces.text: Heavenly Father, thank you for your word today. Do not let the worries of the week choke what was planted in us today. Bring it back to mind when we need it, at home and at work, and make us “doers of the word, and not hearers only” (James 1:22). In Jesus’ name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers and Benedictions for a Church Service

pieces.text: Lord Jesus, you have fed us here, and now you send us out. Open our eyes to the needs of the people we will meet this week, and give us willing hands to meet them. Let each of us use the gift you have given, “as good stewards of the manifold grace of God” (1 Peter 4:10). “Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven” (Matthew 5:16). Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers and Benedictions for a Church Service

pieces.text:
Lord of Light, we have gathered in your presence and felt the warmth of your love. Now you send us out into a world that is longing for hope. We know there is darkness—confusion, sorrow, and despair. But you have called us to be a light. Father, we ask for the boldness to shine for you.

Help us to live in a way that makes people ask about the hope that is within us. As your Word says in Matthew 5:16, "let your light shine before others, that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven." May our lives be the good deeds that point directly back to You. Let our kindness be a beacon.

Don't let us hide what you've given us, but empower us to illuminate the dark corners of the world, In Jesus' Name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers and Benedictions for a Church Service

pieces.text:
Almighty God, our Rock and our Fortress, we thank you for this time of rest and renewal in your house. Now, as we look toward the coming week, we know that we will face trials and temptations. Our own strength is not enough. We ask you to fill us with your supernatural strength and unshakeable courage.

When we feel weak, be our power. When we feel afraid, be our confidence. Remind us of your promise in Isaiah 41:10: "So do not fear, for I am with you; do not be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you and help you; I will uphold you with my righteous right hand." Stand beside us in every meeting, every conversation, and every difficult decision.

May we walk through this week not in our own power, but in the mighty power that comes only from you, In Jesus' Name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers and Benedictions for a Church Service

pieces.text: Lord God, we have come in from a week of work, worry and ordinary things, and we are here because you called us. Quiet our minds. Open our ears to your Word and our mouths to your praise. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for Church Service: Short Invocations to Read Aloud

pieces.text: Holy Spirit, without you this is only a meeting. Come and do what we cannot do ourselves: make the Scriptures plain, turn our singing into praise and our requests into real prayer. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for Church Service: Short Invocations to Read Aloud

pieces.text: Father, thank you for this day and for bringing us here. Thank you for the people sitting beside us, for the food we ate this morning and the breath we sing with. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for Church Service: Short Invocations to Read Aloud

pieces.text: Lord Jesus, you prayed for your followers "that they all may be one" (John 17:21). We come in this morning with our differences: young and old, new and long-standing, some who agree about everything and some who do not. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for Church Service: Short Invocations to Read Aloud

pieces.text: Lord, speak through the one who preaches today. Keep the preacher faithful to your Word and free from the fear of people. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for Church Service: Short Invocations to Read Aloud

pieces.text: O Almighty God, who pourest out on all who desire it, the spirit of grace and of supplication; Deliver us, when we draw nigh to thee, from coldness of heart and wanderings of mind, that with stedfast thoughts and kindled affections, we may worship thee in spirit and in truth; through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.
pieces.source: The Book of Common Prayer (1928), Family Prayer, "For the Spirit of Prayer," p. 594

pieces.text: O God, who hast promised that in all places where Thou dost record Thy Name, Thou wilt meet with Thy servants to bless them; Fulfil now Thy promise, and make us joyful in Thy house of prayer; that our worship, being offered in the Name of Thy Son and by the guidance of Thy Spirit, may be acceptable unto Thee, and profitable unto ourselves; through our only Mediator and Advocate, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.
pieces.source: The Book of Common Worship (Presbyterian Church in the U.S.A.), 1906, Morning Service, The Invocation, p. 3

pieces.text: Lord God, we have come in from a week of work, worry and ordinary things, and we are here because you called us. Quiet our minds. Open our ears to your Word and our mouths to your praise. Let everything said and sung this morning be true, and let it honor Jesus Christ, in whose name we pray. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for Church Service: Short Invocations to Read Aloud

pieces.text: Holy Spirit, without you this is only a meeting. Come and do what we cannot do ourselves: make the Scriptures plain, turn our singing into praise and our requests into real prayer. Where any heart here is cold or tired this morning, warm it. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for Church Service: Short Invocations to Read Aloud

pieces.text: Father, thank you for this day and for bringing us here. Thank you for the people sitting beside us, for the food we ate this morning and the breath we sing with. Every good thing we have came from you. Receive our thanks and our worship, through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for Church Service: Short Invocations to Read Aloud

pieces.text: Lord, thank you for the passage we read and for each person who came tonight. Let what we learned stay with us past the door. Keep safe those who asked for prayer, and bring us back together next week. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers for a Church Meeting: Committees, Small Groups and the Grace

pieces.text: Heavenly Father, thank you for bringing us together today, for every idea that was shared and for the patience we showed each other. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers for a Meeting: Short Prayers and Traditional Blessings to Read Aloud

pieces.text:
Dear Lord,

We thank you for the blessing of your word and for the opportunity to gather together in fellowship.

We ask these things in Jesus' name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers & Verses to Conclude Bible Study Gatherings

pieces.text: Lord, thank you for the passage we read and for each person who came tonight. Let what we learned stay with us past the door. Keep safe those who asked for prayer, and bring us back together next week. “In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you” (1 Thessalonians 5:18). Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers for a Church Meeting: Committees, Small Groups and the Grace

pieces.text: Heavenly Father, thank you for bringing us together today, for every idea that was shared and for the patience we showed each other. Thank you for being with us, as you promised, where two or three are gathered in your name. Send us home grateful. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Closing Prayers for a Meeting: Short Prayers and Traditional Blessings to Read Aloud

pieces.text: We pray for Your guidance and understanding as we seek to deepen our knowledge of Your teachings. Help us to understand the scriptures with open hearts and minds, and to apply Your teaching to our lives. Give us the courage to stand firm in our faith, trust in You, and be faithful. May we always turn to You for wisdom, and may our study of Your Word lead us closer to You. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers & Verses to Conclude Bible Study Gatherings

pieces.text: We thank You for the privilege of coming together to study Your word and learn from it. We praise You for Your love, mercy, and kindness. You have blessed us with life and faith and we are thankful. We also thank You for the opportunities You have given us to serve You and help others in need. May all that we do bring glory to Your name. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers & Verses to Conclude Bible Study Gatherings

pieces.text:
Dear Lord,

We thank you for the blessing of your word and for the opportunity to gather together in fellowship. We thank you for the calling to share your love and grace with the world. pieces.text:
Dear Lord,

We thank you for the blessing of your word and for the opportunity to gather together in fellowship. We thank you for the calling to share your love and grace with the world. Help us to be your humble servants, sharing your message of hope and salvation with those around us. Give us courage and boldness to speak your truth and to be examples of your love. We pray for those who do not yet know you, that you would open their eyes to the truth of your word and draw them into your loving embrace.

We ask these things in Jesus' name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers & Verses to Conclude Bible Study Gatherings

pieces.text: We thank You for the gift of Your word and the opportunity to study it. We recognize that only through Your grace and power can we gain spiritual enlightenment. Help us to open our hearts and minds to Your truth and to seek Your will for our lives. Empower us to become spiritually enlightened and bring us closer to You. May our understanding of Your word bring us peace and joy and strengthen our faith. We ask this in Your name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers & Verses to Conclude Bible Study Gatherings

pieces.text: We thank You for the opportunity to come together, to learn from one another, and to grow in faith. We ask that You will bless this time, create a spirit of unity among us, and open our words and hearts to one another. Help us to speak with respect and understanding, and to listen with humility and compassion. May we be reminded of our common humanity and our love for You. We ask for Your divine guidance, that we may learn from each other and be blessed in our time together. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers & Verses to Conclude Bible Study Gatherings

pieces.text: Heavenly Father, thank You for the gift of Your word. We are so privileged to be able to open Your book and learn about the mystery and wonder of Your love. We thank You for all the lessons and knowledge You have graciously given us. Help us to remember what we learned today, and to apply it to our lives. Help us remember to stay humble and have faith, even in the darkest times. And give us the courage to share Your truth with those around us. In Jesus' name, we pray. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers & Verses to Conclude Bible Study Gatherings

pieces.text:
Lord Jesus, we thank you for our time together to learn and grow in faith. You have blessed us with love and wisdom and we ask that you continue to lead us in our lives. May your presence fill our hearts and bring peace and joy to our souls.

Help us to trust in your will and to lean into your Word as we strive to follow your teachings. We pray that we can solace in your grace and mercy when we feel overwhelmed or lost. We thank you for this day and ask that you bless us and our families. In your name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Prayers & Verses to Conclude Bible Study Gatherings

pieces.text: Lord, our hands are open and our ears are open. Fill them with what you want to give us today. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for Sunday School: For Kids, Adults and Teachers

pieces.text: Father, thank you for bringing us together around your word. Open our minds to understand it and our hearts to receive it. Where we disagree, keep us patient and kind with one another. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for Bible Study: Short Prayers to Read Aloud

pieces.text: Lord, some of what we read today will be hard to follow. Send your Holy Spirit, who Jesus promised “will guide you into all truth” (John 16:13). In Jesus’ name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for Bible Study: Short Prayers to Read Aloud

pieces.text: Lord, some of us are meeting for the first time. Help us learn one another’s names and make everyone welcome. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for Bible Study: Short Prayers to Read Aloud

pieces.text: Father, we have come to study your word together. Clear our minds of the week’s business and the conversations we had on the way in. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for Sunday School: For Kids, Adults and Teachers

pieces.text: God, some of us come with questions and doubts, and some with settled answers. Give us patience with each other, the humility to listen before we speak, and the courage to say what we really think. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for Sunday School: For Kids, Adults and Teachers

pieces.text: Blessed Lord, who hast caused all holy Scriptures to be written for our learning; Grant that we may in such wise hear them, read, mark, learn, and inwardly digest them, that by patience and comfort of thy holy Word, we may embrace, and ever hold fast, the blessed hope of everlasting life, which thou hast given us in our Saviour Jesus Christ. Amen.
pieces.source: The Book of Common Prayer (1928), The Second Sunday in Advent, The Collect, p. 92

pieces.text: Grant, O Lord, that by thy holy Word which shall be read and preached in this place, and by thy Holy Spirit grafting it inwardly in the heart, the hearers thereof may both perceive and know what things they ought to do, and may have power and strength to fulfil the same. Amen.
pieces.source: The Book of Common Prayer (1928), The Form of Consecration of a Church or Chapel, p. 566

pieces.text: Almighty God, our heavenly Father, who hast committed to thy holy Church the care and nurture of thy children; Enlighten with thy wisdom those who teach and those who learn, that, rejoicing in the knowledge of thy truth, they may worship thee and serve thee from generation to generation; through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.
pieces.source: The Book of Common Prayer (1928), Prayers, “For Religious Education,” p. 42

pieces.text: Father, thank you for bringing us together around your word. Open our minds to understand it and our hearts to receive it. Where we disagree, keep us patient and kind with one another. Let what we read tonight change the way we live this week. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for Bible Study: Short Prayers to Read Aloud

pieces.text: Father, we have come to study your word together. Clear our minds of the week’s business and the conversations we had on the way in. Open our understanding, as your Son opened the understanding of his disciples “that they might understand the scriptures” (Luke 24:45). Let what we learn change how we live this week. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for Sunday School: For Kids, Adults and Teachers

pieces.text: God, some of us come with questions and doubts, and some with settled answers. Give us patience with each other, the humility to listen before we speak, and the courage to say what we really think. Keep our talk kind and our study faithful to your word. Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for Sunday School: For Kids, Adults and Teachers

pieces.text: Lord God, thank you for speaking to us. Thank you for the people who wrote these books, for those who copied and translated them, and for those who taught them to us. We have your word in our own language, in our hands, to read as often as we like. Do not let us take that for granted. “Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path” (Psalm 119:105): light our way tonight as we read. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for Bible Study: Short Prayers to Read Aloud

pieces.text: Heavenly Father, we come to your word as learners. Some of us have read these pages for years and some are opening them for the first time, and all of us have more to learn. Take away any pride that makes us think we already know what a passage says. Give us the humility to be corrected by your word, and to learn from one another around this table, whoever is speaking. Your word says to “receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls” (James 1:21). Plant it deep in us today. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for Bible Study: Short Prayers to Read Aloud

pieces.text: Father, we do not want to finish this study knowing more facts and loving you no more than before. Show us yourself in these pages: your holiness, your mercy and your faithfulness, and above all your Son. You promised, “ye shall seek me, and find me, when ye shall search for me with all your heart” (Jeremiah 29:13). Where our lives do not match what we read, change us. Make us “transformed by the renewing of your mind” (Romans 12:2), in our words, our habits and the way we treat people. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
pieces.source: From our article: Opening Prayers for Bible Study: Short Prayers to Read Aloud

pieces.text: Incomprehensible Creator, the true Fountain of light and only Author of all knowledge: vouchsafe, we beseech Thee, to enlighten our understandings, and to remove from us all darkness of sin and ignorance. [Thou, who makest eloquent the tongues of those that want utterance, direct our tongues, and pour on our lips the grace of Thy blessing.] Give us a diligent and obedient spirit, quickness of apprehension, capacity of retaining, and the powerful assistance of Thy holy grace; that what we hear or learn we may apply to Thy honor and the eternal salvation of our own souls.
pieces.source: A Manual of Prayers for the Use of the Catholic Laity (1888), Occasional Prayers, “A Prayer before Study or Instructions,” pp. 171–172
